Because only He can take a divided heart—
and make it whole again.
Only He can turn pride into surrender.
Only He can turn shame into redemption.
This is your moment.
Not tomorrow.
Not someday.
Now.
If this hit your heart—
Respond.
Engage.
Move.
If this stirred something deep in you…
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: He built something no one would question.
paragraphs:
He built something no one would question.
And that was the problem.

Because the most dangerous sin…
is the one that looks successful.

Shebna wasn’t weak.
He was influential. Positioned. Trusted.

But while a nation stood on the edge of collapse…
he was busy securing his legacy.

Isaiah records it with surgical precision—God confronts him: “What have you to do here… that you have cut out here a tomb for yourself?” (Isaiah 22:16).
A monument.
A name etched in stone.
A life built to be remembered.
But not by God.
And here’s the open wound most won’t touch:

You can be active in God’s house…
and still be building your own.

Serving—but seen.
Giving—but noticed.
Leading—but secretly craving applause.

Not because you’re evil.
But because something inside you still wants to be exalted.
Read that again.

This isn’t just Shebna’s story.
This is the quiet war inside people who love God… but still love recognition.

The applause you didn’t admit you needed.
The obedience you delayed because it wouldn’t be seen.
The “yes” you gave publicly… but wrestled with privately.
And no one knows.
Except God.

Because Scripture says in Proverbs 16:18, “Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.”
Not after. Before.

Meaning—your fall doesn’t start when you collapse.
It starts when you crown yourself.
AHA REVELATION:

Pride doesn’t always shout.
Sometimes it whispers, “You deserve this.”
And that whisper builds tombs.

Shebna wasn’t judged for laziness.
He was judged for self-exaltation.

God says in Isaiah 22:19, “I will thrust you from your office… you will be pulled down.”
Not because he had no role—
but because he forgot who gave it.
SPIRITUAL MIRROR:

Are you building something for God…
or building something out of God?
Sit with that.

Because some of us don’t need more opportunities.
We need purification.

There are prayers you’ve been praying…
that God is delaying—not because He’s silent,
but because your heart isn’t ready to carry what you’re asking for.
That’s mercy.
Because unchecked pride can turn blessings into idols.
And here’s the piercing truth:
God will remove what you misuse.

Even if it’s ministry.
Even if it’s influence.
Even if it’s something you once received from Him.

That’s not cruelty.
That’s holiness.
But here’s where grace breaks in.
Because the story doesn’t end with removal.
Right after Shebna… God raises Eliakim. A faithful servant. And then Scripture keeps unfolding until we meet Jesus—the true and better One.

Where Shebna built a tomb for himself…
Jesus walked toward a tomb for us.

Where Shebna tried to secure his name…
Jesus emptied Himself, “taking the form of a servant… humbling Himself to death—even death on a cross” (Philippians 2:7–8).
And here’s the Gospel:
We have all been Shebna.

Romans 3:23 says “all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”
Every hidden motive.
Every quiet pride.
Every moment we wanted the glory that belongs to Him.
But God didn’t just expose our pride.
He paid for it.
On the cross, Jesus took the weight of our self-exaltation… and offered us something we could never build:
Grace.
Ephesians 2:8–9 makes it clear—“by grace you have been saved through faith… not a result of works, so that no one may boast.”

No monuments.
No self-made identity.
No earned glory.
Just mercy.
This is your turning point.

Not to try harder.
Not to perform better.
But to surrender deeper.

Lay down the need to be seen.
Lay down the craving for recognition.
Lay down the subtle pride that dresses itself as calling.
Because you were not created to build your name.
You were created to carry His.
Identity shift:

You are not the architect of your own glory.
You are a vessel of His grace.

And vessels don’t boast.
They overflow.
So come back.
Quietly. Honestly.
Repent—not just of sin… but of self.
Let Jesus take the throne you’ve been slowly reclaiming.

Because the safest place in the world…
is not at the top.
It’s surrendered.
If this is hitting deeper than expected, stay a little longer.

And something else is coming next…
because Shebna is not the only one we’ve overlooked.
Someone close to you is fighting a silent version of this.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Most people think the cross was the final moment.
paragraphs: Most people think the cross was the final moment.
It wasn’t.
Something else happened… quietly, violently, and almost hidden from public view.
Inside the temple—far from the crowds, far from the noise of Golgotha—there stood a veil.

Massive.
Heavy.
Sacred.
It wasn’t just fabric.
It was a boundary.
This veil separated the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place—the very dwelling place of God’s presence (Exodus 26:33).
No one walked in there casually.
No one wandered in out of curiosity.

Only the high priest could enter.
Once a year.
With blood.
And even then, not without fear (Hebrews 9:7).
Because that veil was a message:
“God is holy… and you are not.”
Now imagine the moment.
Jesus is hanging on the cross.

His body is torn.
His breath is fading.
The sky grows dark.
And then—He cries out…
“It is finished.” (John 19:30)
And He gives up His spirit.
At that exact moment…
The veil tears.

Not slowly.
Not symbolically.
Not from the bottom—like a human would do.
From top… to bottom. (Matthew 27:51)
God did it.
This wasn’t just a miracle.
It was an announcement.
Heaven was declaring something that would redefine humanity’s relationship with God forever.
Here’s the truth most people miss:
The veil didn’t exist to keep people from God…
It existed to protect people from His holiness.
Because sin and holiness cannot coexist.
So the veil stood as both a barrier and a mercy.
But when Jesus died, everything changed.
Because the cross didn’t just deal with sin…
It satisfied justice.
It fulfilled the law.
It completed the requirement for atonement once and for all (Hebrews 10:12).
And so the veil was no longer needed.
Not because God became less holy…
But because through Christ, we can now stand before Him.
Let that sink in.

The place that once required fear…
Now invites intimacy.

The presence that once demanded distance…
Now welcomes you near.
But here’s where it gets personal.
Many people today still live like the veil is intact.

They pray like God is far.
They worship like they’re unworthy to come close.
They carry guilt that Jesus already paid for.

They stand outside…
Even though the door is gone.
The veil didn’t tear halfway.
God didn’t say, “Come closer… but not too close.”
He tore it completely.
Access wasn’t partially granted.
It was fully opened.
But access doesn’t mean casual.
This is where we must be careful.
The tearing of the veil was free for us…
But it was not cheap.
It cost the blood of Jesus.
So yes—you can come boldly (Hebrews 4:16).
But never carelessly.
Because the same God who invites you in…
Is still holy.
Here’s the deeper lesson:

Jesus didn’t just open a way…
He became the way. (John 14:6)
There is no longer a curtain.
There is no longer a system of barriers.
There is no longer a human mediator standing between you and God.
Christ is your access.
Christ is your covering.
Christ is your High Priest.
And this changes everything about how you live.

You don’t pray to be heard—you’re already invited.
You don’t worship to earn presence—you’re already in it.
You don’t strive for acceptance—you already have it in Christ.
But the real question is not:
“Did the veil tear?”
It did.
The real question is:
Why are you still standing outside?
Why live distant when access has been granted?
Why carry shame when forgiveness has been completed?
Why act like God is unreachable…
When He is now near?
Some people are waiting for a sign.
The veil was the sign.
Some people are waiting to feel worthy.
Jesus made you worthy through His sacrifice.
So stop knocking on a door that no longer exists.
Step in.
Draw near.
Live like the veil is truly gone.
Because it is.

“The veil was torn, but many still live separated.”
“Access to God is not earned—it was given through sacrifice.”
“You are not standing outside because you’re unworthy… but because you haven’t stepped in.”
The cross didn’t just forgive you.
It brought you close.

Engagement Question:
Do you truly live like you have direct access to God—or do you still feel like you’re standing outside the veil?
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: He sounded like God…
paragraphs:
He sounded like God…
but died without Him.
Pause.
Let that sink in.

Because this is not just his story.
This could be yours.

He was brilliant.
Respected.
Unmatched in insight.
When Ahithophel spoke, kings leaned in.
Scripture says:
“The counsel that Ahithophel gave was as if one consulted the word of God.” — 2 Samuel 16:23

Not good advice.
Not wise suggestions.
The voice of God—that’s how people received him.
And yet…

He ended his life alone, undone, hanging in silence.
— 2 Samuel 17:23
So what happened?
Here’s the tension you don’t want to face:

You can be spiritually impressive…
and still be spiritually dead.

You can know Scripture…
and not know the Savior.

You can guide others…
while your own soul is drifting into darkness.
Let’s go deeper.
Ahithophel didn’t just fail.
He chose sides.
When Absalom rebelled against King David, Ahithophel—David’s trusted advisor—betrayed him.
Why?
The Bible doesn’t spell out every motive.

But many scholars connect Ahithophel to Bathsheba’s family line (2 Samuel 11; 23:34).
Some scholars interpret that his betrayal may have been fueled by unresolved bitterness from David’s sin.
Think about that.
A wound.
A grudge.
A silent fire burning beneath polished wisdom.
And here’s where it gets dangerously relatable.

You can carry pain so long…
that it starts to justify your pride.

You can nurture offense so deeply…
that it begins to rewrite your loyalty.
You don’t fall overnight.
You drift.
Quietly.
Respectably.
Ahithophel’s wisdom remained sharp.
But his heart turned cold.
And when his counsel was rejected?
He didn’t repent.
He didn’t pause.
He didn’t seek God.
He chose control over surrender.
Scripture says:
“When Ahithophel saw that his counsel was not followed, he saddled his donkey… set his house in order, and hanged himself.” — 2 Samuel 17:23
Read that slowly.
He prepared everything externally…
But inside?
He was already gone.
This is the danger of pride.
Not loud arrogance.
But quiet self-trust.
The kind that says:

“I know what’s right.”
“I see clearly.”
“I don’t need correction.”
Listen carefully.
Pride doesn’t always look like rebellion.
Sometimes it looks like being right… without being surrendered.
And this is where the Gospel breaks in.
Because Ahithophel’s story doesn’t end with hope…
But yours still can.
There is another Counselor.
Not one who sounds like God…
But One who is God.
Jesus Christ.
Scripture declares:
“Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God.” — 1 Corinthians 1:24
Not borrowed wisdom.
Not perceived authority.
He is Wisdom Himself.
Ahithophel gave advice that shaped kingdoms.
Jesus gives words that raise the dead inside you.
Ahithophel’s voice influenced kings.
Jesus’ voice forgives sinners.
And here’s the Gospel truth:
Your greatest problem is not ignorance.
It’s sin.
The hidden pride.
The quiet rebellion.
The moments you chose yourself over God.
And the solution is not becoming wiser.
It’s becoming surrendered.
Because no amount of insight can save you.
Only Jesus can.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23

That includes the wise.
The respected.
The admired.
But here is the explosion of grace:
“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
Not when you fixed yourself.
Not when you became worthy.
But while you were still broken…
Christ stepped in.
And unlike Ahithophel—who ended in despair—
Jesus entered death and conquered it.
So no one has to end where pride leads.
This is your moment.
Right here.
Right now.
Where is pride hiding in your life?

In your opinions?
Your wounds?
Your silent judgments?
Your need to be right?
Don’t wait until rejection exposes what humility could have healed.
Don’t let hidden pride write your ending.
Come back.
Not to religion.
Not to performance.
To Jesus.
Lay down your need to control.
Lay down your need to be right.
Lay down the version of yourself you’ve been protecting.
And receive grace.
Real grace.

The kind that humbles you…
and heals you.
“God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.” — James 4:6
That’s the dividing line.
Not intelligence.
Not influence.
Humility.
So choose it.
Right now.
If this pierced your heart…
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: He thought death was the end.
paragraphs: He thought death was the end.
But what followed him… was worse.
You see it, don’t you?
That moment.
That look over the shoulder.
That breath caught between panic and realization.
Because deep down… he knows something is coming.
And he can’t outrun it.
We live like that man more than we admit.

We scroll.
We laugh.
We distract.

But there are moments—quiet ones—
when your soul whispers:
“This isn’t right.”

That hidden habit.
That private compromise.
That thing no one knows.
Or so you think.
Sin doesn’t knock loudly at first.
It whispers.

Soft.
Reasonable.
Justified.

“Just once.”
“Just this time.”
“No one will find out.”
But sin doesn’t stay small.
It grows.
It follows.
It rides.
Revelation pulls the curtain back.
“And I looked, and behold a pale horse: and his name that sat on him was Death, and Hell followed with him…” — Revelation 6:8 (KJV)
Death rides.
Hell follows.
Not separately.
Together.
Relentless.
Some scholars interpret the pale horse as symbolic of widespread judgment—war, famine, disease, and chaos unleashed in a world that has rejected God.
But don’t miss this—
It’s not just about the end of the world.
It’s a mirror of what sin does in the human heart.
James writes it plainly:
Did you catch the progression?

Desire.
Sin.
Death.
It always ends there.
Always.
That’s the part we try to ignore.

We want the pleasure without the consequence.
The thrill without the cost.
The secret without the exposure.
But sin is never satisfied staying hidden.

It follows you into your thoughts.
Your relationships.
Your identity.
Until one day—
You look back…
And realize something is chasing you.
And here’s the hardest truth:
You cannot outrun death.

You cannot outwork your guilt.
You cannot out-religion your sin.
You cannot out-hide what God already sees.
“Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight…” — Hebrews 4:13 (KJV)
Everything is exposed.
Everything.
But here’s what will shake you—
Death is not the greatest enemy.
Separation from God is.
Jesus said:
“And fear not them which kill the body… but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.” — Matthew 10:28 (KJV)
This is bigger than physical death.
This is eternal.
Now pause.
Because this is where everything changes.
The story doesn’t end with a horse.
It ends with a cross.
Jesus stepped into the path of death.
Not as a victim.
As a substitute.
“For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin…” — 2 Corinthians 5:21 (KJV)
He took what was chasing you.
He carried what was condemning you.
He absorbed the judgment meant for you.
The pale horse rides with death.
But Jesus walked out of the grave with keys.
“I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore… and have the keys of hell and of death.” — Revelation 1:18 (KJV)
Keys.
Authority.
Final say.
So now the question is not:
“Is death coming?”
It is.
The question is—
Who holds your eternity?
Because without Christ…
Death is not the end.
It’s the beginning of separation.
But in Christ…
Death is defeated.
“O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory?” — 1 Corinthians 15:55 (KJV)
This is your moment.
Not later.
Not someday.
Now.
That thing you’ve been hiding?
Bring it into the light.
That sin you’ve been justifying?
Lay it down.
That distance between you and God?
Close it.
Repent.
Not just feel bad.
Turn.
Run to Jesus.
Not slowly.
Not casually.
Urgently.
Because grace is not chasing you to condemn you.
It’s chasing you to save you.
“The Lord is… not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.” — 2 Peter 3:9 (KJV)
You are not too far gone.
You are not too dirty.
You are not too late.
The cross already accounted for your worst moment.
But you must respond.
You must choose.
Life… or slow death.
Christ… or separation.
Truth… or denial.
If this hit your heart, don’t ignore it.
This isn’t coincidence.
This is God calling you back.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: She had nothing left to prove.
paragraphs:
She had nothing left to prove.
No spotlight to chase.
No one waiting for her name.
Just a quiet corner… and a lifetime of prayer.

And yet—
Heaven trusted her eyes to recognize the Messiah.
Anna.

A widow.
A woman marked by loss.
A soul that stayed when others moved on.
📖 “She did not depart from the temple, worshiping with fasting and prayer night and day.” — Luke 2:37
Let that sink in.

Not days.
Not weeks.
Years.

Silent years.
Hidden years.
Unseen faithfulness.

No applause.
No validation.
Just devotion.
And if we’re honest—this is where most people quit.

Because waiting without results feels like rejection.
Praying without answers feels like silence.
Serving without recognition feels like being forgotten.
But Anna stayed.
Why?

Because she wasn’t chasing outcomes.
She was anchored in God.

Then one ordinary day…
everything shifted.
A young couple walked into the temple carrying a baby.

No royal garments.
No army escort.
No visible glory.
Just a child wrapped in simplicity.
And here’s the tension—

Everyone saw a baby.
Anna saw the Redeemer.
How?

Because what you train your heart to seek…
you will recognize when it appears.

This is not accidental revelation.
This is cultivated sensitivity.

A life of prayer sharpened her vision.
Fasting cleared her distractions.
Faithfulness aligned her spirit.

So when Jesus came—
she didn’t hesitate.
📖 “Coming up at that very hour she began to give thanks to God and to speak of Him to all who were waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem.” — Luke 2:38
Did you catch that?

She didn’t just recognize Him—
she proclaimed Him.

Before the miracles.
Before the sermons.
Before the cross.
She saw enough in the child Christ to declare:

This is Him.
This is the Promise.
This is the One we’ve been waiting for.
And here’s where it cuts deep.
Some of you are in your “Anna season” right now.

Waiting.
Praying.
Crying in places nobody sees.
Wondering if your faithfulness even matters.
Let me speak this straight:
God is not wasting your waiting.

Every prayer is shaping perception.
Every hidden moment is training your spirit.
Every tear is preparing you for recognition.

Because when Jesus moves—
you don’t want to miss Him.
And many do.

Not because He isn’t present…
but because their hearts are distracted.
Anna teaches us this:
It is possible to be surrounded by God… and still not see Him.

But it is also possible—
to live so close to His presence
that you recognize Him instantly, even when He comes wrapped in ordinary moments.
Let’s go deeper.
Anna was waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem.

That word—redemption—is not poetic language.
It is costly language.

It means rescue.
It means ransom.
It means someone else pays the price.
And here is the Gospel:

The baby she held her gaze upon
would one day carry a cross.

The tiny hands she saw
would be pierced.

The child she praised
would become the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world (John 1:29).

This is not just a beautiful moment.
This is a prophetic encounter.

Anna wasn’t just seeing a child—
she was witnessing the beginning of salvation.

For sinners.
For the broken.
For the ashamed.
For us.
So the question is not just:
Did Anna recognize Jesus?
The real question is:
Do you?

Do you recognize Him in your waiting?
In your unanswered prayers?
In your quiet, hidden seasons?

Or are you looking for something louder…
more dramatic…
more convenient?

Because Jesus often comes quietly.
Humbly.
Unexpectedly.

And only those who are watching—
really watching—
will see Him.

If you feel unseen today…
if your prayers feel repetitive…
if your faith feels unnoticed…
Stay.

Stay in His presence.
Stay in prayer.
Stay in worship.

Because one moment with Jesus
will redeem every year you thought was wasted.

And when He reveals Himself—
you will know.

Not because the world told you…
but because your spirit was trained to see Him.
Remind them:
God sees. God hears. God comes.

And when He does—
may we be like Anna.

Ready.
Awake.
Recognizing.
“We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.”
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: You thought your story was already decided.
paragraphs:
You thought your story was already decided.
The mistakes. The nights no one saw. The quiet guilt that follows you even when everything looks fine on the outside.
But listen—this will shake you if you let it.
Your ending has already been claimed… by Someone stronger than your past.
“I am the Alpha and the Omega,” says the Lord God, “who is, and who was, and who is to come, the Almighty.” (Revelation 1:8)

Not “I was.”
Not “I might be.”
Not “I’m trying to fix things.”
I AM.

Alpha.
The beginning.

Omega.
The end.

That means before your first breath—He was already there.
And long after your last heartbeat—He will still be God.
So why are you living like everything depends on you?
Why are you carrying a weight you were never meant to hold?
Some of you are exhausted… not because life is heavy—but because you’re trying to be your own Alpha and Omega.

You’re trying to start your own healing.
You’re trying to control your own outcome.
You’re trying to rewrite your own story.
And it’s breaking you.
Because only God can stand at both ends of time and say, “I hold it all together.”
Here’s the truth most people avoid:
Sin makes us forget who is really in control.

It whispers lies like—
“You’ve gone too far.”
“You’ve ruined everything.”
“There’s no coming back from this.”
But the Gospel answers louder.

The Alpha stepped into our broken beginning.
The Omega stepped into our deserved ending.
Jesus Christ—fully God, fully man—entered time, took on flesh, and walked into our mess without flinching. He didn’t avoid sinners. He moved toward them.

Toward liars.
Toward addicts.
Toward the ashamed.
Toward the ones hiding behind curated lives and silent regrets.
And then the unthinkable happened.
He took the weight of sin—your sin, my sin—upon Himself.
At the cross, it looked like the end.

Darkness.
Blood.
Silence.
Hope seemed buried.
But three days later—
The Omega rewrote the ending.

The tomb opened.
Death lost its grip.
Jesus rose—not as a symbol—but as a living, victorious Savior.
And that changes everything.
Because now, the One who holds the end… offers you a new beginning.
Let that sink in.

Your failure is not final.
Your shame is not sovereign.
Your past is not your master.
Jesus is.
And He doesn’t just observe your story—He redeems it.
Some scholars interpret Revelation 1:8 as both a declaration of God’s eternal nature and a direct affirmation of Christ’s divine authority. Either way, the message stands unshaken:
The One who began all things will also bring them to completion.
So if you are in Christ, your life is not spiraling—it is being shaped.

Even the pain.
Even the delay.
Even the seasons that make no sense.

He is Alpha there.
He is Omega there.
Which means—

There is purpose in your waiting.
There is mercy in your correction.
There is hope beyond what you can currently see.
But don’t miss this:

Grace is not automatic.
It is received.

Not earned.
Not performed for.
Not negotiated.
Received through repentance and faith in Jesus alone.

Turn from sin.
Trust in Christ.
Surrender the illusion of control.
Because the same voice that spoke galaxies into existence is calling your name.

Not to condemn you—
but to restore you.

Not to shame you—
but to save you.

Not to end you—
but to begin something brand new.
So here’s the question you can’t ignore:
Who is writing your story right now?

Is it your fear?
Your past?
Your addiction?
Your pride?
Or have you finally surrendered the pen to the Alpha and Omega?
Because one day—every story reaches its final page.
And only one ending leads to life.
Jesus Christ. Crucified. Risen. Reigning.

This is not religion.
This is rescue.
And it’s still available—right now.

Come back.
Even if you feel far.

Come home.
Even if you feel unworthy.

Come to Jesus.
Because the beginning and the end are not against you—
If you belong to Him.

Your story is not over.
It’s being rewritten.
Type “ALPHA & OMEGA” if you believe Jesus holds your story.
Because it’s not.

Not while He is still the Alpha…
and the Omega.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: She didn’t fall when she saw the fruit.
paragraphs:
She didn’t fall when she saw the fruit.
She fell when she listened too long.
And here’s the part that should shake you:

It didn’t feel like sin at first.
It felt like… a conversation.

Curious.
Harmless.
Almost intelligent.
But something was shifting.

Something subtle.
Something dangerous.
And most people never see it coming.
Because the serpent didn’t start with rebellion.
He started with a question.
“Did God really say…?” — Genesis 3:1

Not a command.
Not an attack.
A whisper.
A seed of doubt.
And Eve… stayed.

She didn’t run.
She didn’t rebuke.
She engaged.
And that’s where everything began to unravel.
Let’s get real for a moment.
This is not just Eve’s story.

This is your midnight thought.
Your private scrolling.
Your quiet justifications.
The voice that says:

“It’s not that serious.”
“You deserve this.”
“God understands…”
Sin rarely shows up wearing a name tag.
It comes dressed as reason.
It sounds like logic.
It feels like freedom.
And here’s the shift that most people miss:
Eve didn’t just listen.
She edited God’s Word.
“You must not eat… or touch it…” — Genesis 3:3
But God never said “touch.”

Some scholars interpret this as Eve trying to protect the command—
but in doing so, she added to it.
And when you add to God’s Word…
You open the door to distorting it.
Then the serpent goes deeper.

From question…
to contradiction.
“You will not surely die…” — Genesis 3:4
Now truth is under attack.
And then comes the final blow:
“You will be like God…” — Genesis 3:5
There it is.
Not fruit.
Identity.
This wasn’t about hunger.
It was about becoming something apart from God.
And if we’re honest?
That’s still the temptation today.

To define yourself without Him.
To satisfy yourself without Him.
To live like you don’t need Him.
And here’s the painful truth:
Some of us are not trapped in sin because we’re ignorant.
We’re trapped because we’ve been entertaining the wrong voice.
You didn’t fall overnight.
You drifted through dialogue.

One thought.
One compromise.
One “it’s okay this time.”
But hear this—don’t miss it:
Where Eve stood in a garden and gave in…
Jesus stood in a wilderness and fought back.
“It is written…” — Matthew 4:4
Same strategy from the enemy.
Different response.
Jesus didn’t entertain the lie.
He cut it with truth.
Again and again:

“It is written…” — Matthew 4:7
“It is written…” — Matthew 4:10
Where Eve added to God’s Word…
Jesus stood firmly on it.
Where Eve reached…
Jesus refused.
And because He refused…
You don’t have to remain fallen.
Let’s make the Gospel plain.
Sin is not just what you do.
It’s the moment you choose a voice over God’s truth.
And every one of us has done it.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
But God didn’t leave us in that conversation.
He stepped into it.
Through Jesus.
The cross is not just forgiveness.
It’s interruption.
God breaking into your deception and saying:
“This ends here.”
Jesus took the consequence Eve was warned about:
“The wages of sin is death…” — Romans 6:23
He didn’t just feel it.
He absorbed it.
So that now—
Grace speaks louder than the serpent ever could.
“But the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.” — Romans 6:23
This is your moment.
Right here.
Right now.
What voice have you been entertaining?

The one feeding your pride?
Your secret sin?
Your quiet rebellion?
Or the One calling you back?
You don’t need to debate with the lie anymore.
You need to shut it down.
With truth.
With surrender.
With Jesus.
Repent.
Not as punishment—
But as freedom.
Turn from the voice that’s been leading you away…
And come back to the Voice that died to bring you home.
You are not too far gone.
You are not too deceived.
You are not too late.
The same God who walked into the garden after the fall…
Is walking toward you now.
And He’s not asking for perfection.
He’s asking for your yes.
If this hit your heart—
Respond.
if you’re choosing truth over the lie.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: You can sit in church every Sunday…
paragraphs:
You can sit in church every Sunday…
smile, sing, serve…
and still not know God.

That tension right there?
That’s where this message begins.

Because this is not about attendance.
This is about intimacy.

There’s a quiet danger that doesn’t shout.
It doesn’t scandalize headlines.
It hides in routine.

You raise your hands on cue.
You know when to say “Amen.”
You can finish the pastor’s verses before he does.

But when the music fades…
when the crowd goes home…
when it’s just you and your thoughts—
God feels distant.

Not absent in theory.
But absent in experience.
Jesus confronted this exact reality.

“These people honor Me with their lips,
but their hearts are far from Me.” — Matthew 15:8
Read that again.

Not rebels.
Not atheists.
Not outsiders.
Church people.

People who looked right…
but loved wrong.

You can master the language of faith
and still be a stranger to the God you speak about.

You can quote Scripture
and still resist surrender.

You can serve in ministry
and still protect secret sin.
This is the tragedy:

Being close to church…
but far from Christ.
And here’s where it gets uncomfortable.

Because many don’t walk away from God—
they sit near Him… without ever truly coming to Him.

They trade relationship for routine.
Conviction for comfort.
Surrender for control.

And slowly, subtly—
their heart drifts.

Not in one dramatic moment.
But in a thousand small compromises.
But listen, kapatid… don’t miss this.

This is not a message of condemnation.
This is a wake-up call wrapped in grace.

Because the very fact that this stirs something in you—
that uneasy feeling, that quiet conviction—
That’s not rejection.
That’s invitation.
God has never been impressed with perfect attendance.
From Genesis to Revelation, He’s after one thing:
Your heart.

Not your performance.
Not your image.
Not your reputation.
Your heart.

“You will seek Me and find Me
when you seek Me with all your heart.” — Jeremiah 29:13
And here’s the Gospel—the turning point, the lifeline, the fire in the darkness:
You don’t have to fix yourself first.

You don’t have to pretend.
You don’t have to clean up before you come close.

Jesus didn’t die for your polished version.
He died for your real one.

Broken.
Conflicted.
Hiding.

“I am the way, and the truth, and the life.
No one comes to the Father except through Me.” — John 14:6

Not through church attendance.
Not through good works.
Not through religious effort.
Through Jesus alone.
This is where everything changes.

Because knowing God is not about proximity to religion—
it’s about surrender to a Person.
And His name is Jesus.
So what does it actually look like to know Him?

It looks like repentance—
not just saying sorry, but turning around.

It looks like obedience—
not perfection, but direction.

It looks like hunger—
a desire for Him that goes beyond Sunday.

It looks like intimacy—
talking to Him, walking with Him, trusting Him in the quiet places.
And yes… it will cost you something.

Your pride.
Your hidden sins.
Your need to stay in control.
But what you gain?
Everything.

Forgiveness that is complete.
Grace that is undeserved.
A relationship that is alive.
Maybe you’ve been in church for years.
Maybe you know all the right things.

But deep down…
you know something is missing.
This is your moment.
Not to try harder.
But to come closer.
Right now, you can pray.

Not a performance prayer.
Not a memorized script.
Just real.

“Lord, I don’t want to just go through the motions anymore.
I want to know You.
Forgive me. Change me. Lead me.
I surrender my life to You.”
And He will meet you there.

Not with shame.
Not with rejection.
But with open arms.
Because that’s who Jesus is.

So don’t settle for being near the things of God
and missing the heart of God.
Don’t trade relationship for routine.
Don’t let familiarity replace fire.
Come back.
Not to religion.
But to Jesus.
Start a conversation.

Because someone out there is sitting in a pew…
feeling exactly this…
and waiting for a wake-up call.

From ritual to relationship.
From distance to intimacy.
From religion to redemption.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: You’re not struggling with sin…
paragraphs: You’re not struggling with sin…
You’re protecting it.
And that changes everything.

Because it’s not just a mistake anymore.
It’s not just weakness.
It’s something you’ve started to defend… justify… even hide behind.
And deep down—
You know it.

There’s a voice in you that whispers,
“This isn’t right.”

But there’s another voice—louder, more persuasive—
“Just one more time.”
“No one will know.”
“You can stop anytime.”
So you stay.

Half-free.
Half-bound.
Half-alive.
Let’s be honest.

You still pray…
But not about that.

You still worship…
But there’s a distance now.

You still say “God is good”…
But your private life is quietly contradicting your public confession.
This is the tension.
This is the war.
And it’s exhausting.
Because secret sin doesn’t just break God’s law…
It slowly breaks you.

It numbs your conviction.
Blurs your identity.
Distorts your desires.

What once convicted you…
Now comforts you.

What once grieved you…
Now entertains you.
And here’s the dangerous part:
You’re getting used to it.

“But each person is tempted when they are dragged away by their own evil desire and enticed. Then, after desire has conceived, it gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is full-grown, gives birth to death.”
— James 1:14–15
That verse is not poetry.
It’s a warning.
A process.
A progression.

Desire.
Then sin.
Then death.
Not always instant death—
But slow death.

Death to your sensitivity.
Death to your fire.
Death to your closeness with God.
Some scholars interpret this “death” not just as physical, but as spiritual separation—a life that exists, but is no longer fully alive in God’s presence.
And maybe that’s where you are right now.
Breathing…
But distant.
Functioning…
But empty.
Smiling…
But hiding.
Because this is where grace enters.
You don’t need a better strategy.
You don’t need more discipline alone.
You need a Savior.
Because sin is not just behavior.
It’s bondage.
And no one breaks chains by willpower alone.
This is why Jesus came.
Not to make you religious—
But to make you free.

“Everyone who sins is a slave to sin… So if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed.”
— John 8:34, 36
Read that again.
Slave.

That thing you keep returning to?
That “small” compromise?
It’s not just something you do.
It’s something that’s starting to own you.
But Jesus doesn’t negotiate with sin.
He crushes it.
At the cross—
Your sin wasn’t ignored.
It was paid for.

Every hidden habit.
Every secret click.
Every private compromise.
All of it—
Placed on Him.

“He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, that we might die to sin and live to righteousness.”
— 1 Peter 2:24
Notice that:
Not just forgiven…
But freed to live differently.
This is the Gospel:

You are more sinful than you want to admit…
But more loved than you ever imagined.
Jesus didn’t die so you could keep managing sin in the shadows.
He died so you could bring it into the light—and be transformed.

“If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.”
— 1 John 1:9
Not shame you.
Not expose you to destroy you.
But cleanse you.
So why are you still holding on?
What are you afraid of losing?
The pleasure?
The escape?
The control?
Listen carefully:
That sin you’re clinging to…
Is already costing you more than it’s giving you.
And Jesus is standing here—
Not with condemnation…
But with open hands.
“Let it go.”
Not because He wants to restrict you—
But because He wants to restore you.
Right now.
Not tomorrow.
Not “when you feel ready.”
Now.
Drop it.
Confess it.
Bring it into the light.
Say it plainly:

“Jesus, I’ve been holding onto this sin.
I’m done hiding.
I repent.
I surrender.
I need You to set me free.”
And He will.
Not partially.
Not temporarily.
Completely.
This is your moment.
Not to feel guilty—
But to come home.
If this pierced your heart, don’t ignore it.
That’s not emotion.
That’s conviction.
And listen—
If this stirred something deep in you…
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: They weren’t just baking bread.
paragraphs:
They weren’t just baking bread.
They were breathing in the stench of their own sin.
Pause.
Because this isn’t just Ezekiel’s story.
It’s yours.
It’s mine.
God told a prophet to cook food over dung.
Not as shock value.
As truth.
Unfiltered.
Uncomfortable.
Unavoidable.

What if what you’ve normalized…
Heaven calls defiled?
What if the thing you’ve been hiding, managing, renaming…
God already exposed?
Ezekiel didn’t argue theology.
He reacted with grief.
“Ah, Lord God! Behold, I have never defiled myself…” (Ezekiel 4:14)
He knew what this meant.
This wasn’t just about food.
This was about identity.
Purity.
Holiness.
And God’s message hit like thunder—
“My people will eat defiled bread among the nations…” (Ezekiel 4:13)
Translation?
Sin doesn’t stay hidden.
It stains.
It spreads.
It seeps into everything.
Let’s get honest.
Some of you aren’t struggling with “big sins.”
You’re just slowly getting used to small compromises.
And they’re cooking your soul.
Quietly.
Daily.
Unnoticed.
That secret habit you defend?
That bitterness you rehearse?
That lust you scroll through at midnight?
That pride you disguise as “confidence”?
That double life you’ve learned to balance?
It doesn’t look dangerous anymore.
But heaven smells it.
And it is not holy.
Sin always starts subtle.
Then it becomes acceptable.
Then it becomes normal.
Then it becomes identity.
Until one day—
You don’t even recognize who you’ve become.
This is the horror of Ezekiel 4.
God was not exaggerating.
He was revealing.
Because sometimes the most loving thing God can do…
Is show you how far you’ve drifted.
And here’s the emotional trigger you can’t escape:
Shame.
Not the fake kind people throw around.
The real kind.
The kind you feel when you’re alone.
When the noise dies.
When distractions fade.
When truth whispers—
“This is not who you were made to be.”
But don’t stop there.
Because if all you see is shame…
You’ve missed the cross.
Now watch this turn.
This is where everything changes.
Ezekiel was told to cook over dung…
But Jesus stepped into a world already covered in it.
He didn’t stand at a distance.
He came close.
He touched lepers (Mark 1:41).
He ate with sinners (Luke 5:30–32).
He walked into places religious people avoided.
Why?
Because defilement doesn’t scare Him.
But pretending does.
And then…
He took it further.
To the cross.
“God made Him who knew no sin to be sin for us…” (2 Corinthians 5:21)
Let that sit.
Jesus didn’t just see your sin.
He carried it.
Every hidden thing.
Every shameful thought.
Every secret compromise.
Every moment you chose darkness over light.
Placed.
On Him.
This is the Gospel.
Not self-improvement.
Not behavior modification.
Not trying harder.
This is substitution.
You deserved the fire.
He took the flame.
You carried the stain.
He became the stain.
So you could become clean.
“Though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be as white as snow…” (Isaiah 1:18)
Not faded.
Not covered.
Washed.
Completely.
But here’s the line most people don’t want to cross:
Repentance.
Not guilt.
Not regret.
Repentance.
A turning.
A surrender.
A decision that says—
“I don’t want to live like this anymore.”
Some scholars interpret Ezekiel 4 as symbolic of Israel’s exile and spiritual corruption.
But the principle stands clear:
Sin defiles.
God confronts.
Grace invites.
So what are you still holding onto?
What are you still calling “not that bad”?
What are you still hiding behind filters and excuses?
Listen carefully.
God is not exposing you to shame you.
He is exposing you to save you.
You don’t need to clean yourself first.
You need to come.
Dirty.
Broken.
Honest.
Because Jesus doesn’t heal fake people.
He heals surrendered ones.
Right now.
Not tomorrow.
Not when you “feel ready.”
Right now.
Say it in your heart if you mean it:
“Jesus, I’m done hiding.”
“I bring You my sin.”
“I receive Your mercy.”
“Make me clean.”
This is your turning point.
Not because you read a post.
But because the Spirit is knocking.
It might be the doorway to freedom.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: They didn’t fall because they didn’t hear.
paragraphs:
They didn’t fall because they didn’t hear.
They fell because they thought hearing was enough.
Let that sink in.

Because this is not about atheists.
Not about rebels.
Not about people far from church.

This is about people…
who sit in the front row.
You’ve felt it before, haven’t you?

That moment in a sermon where your chest tightens.
Where the Word hits too close.
Where you whisper, “Lord… that’s me.”
But then—

You walk out.
You scroll.
You delay.
You distract.
And somehow… you convince yourself:
“I’ll deal with it later.”
Here’s the open wound we don’t talk about:
Delayed obedience is still disobedience.

And the longer it stays delayed,
the quieter your conviction becomes.
Until one day…

You can hear truth
and feel nothing.
Jesus didn’t warn the world about this first.
He warned us.

“Everyone then who hears these words of mine and does them will be like a wise man who built his house on the rock…
And everyone who hears these words of mine and does not do them will be like a foolish man… and great was the fall of it.”
— Matthew 7:24–27

Same words.
Same storm.
Same opportunity.
Different response.
Different ending.
Let’s be honest.
Hearing feels holy.

You attend.
You listen.
You highlight verses.
You repost Christian content.
But obedience?
That’s where it costs.

That’s where pride resists.
That’s where secret sin negotiates.
That’s where the heart says:
“Not yet, Lord.”
And here’s the danger no one tells you:

The more you hear without obeying,
the more you train your heart
to resist God’s voice.
Not loudly.
Subtly.
Quietly.
Dangerously.
“Be doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves.”
Deceiving.
Not confused.
Not ignorant.
Self-deceived.
This is the most dangerous place to be spiritually:

Close to truth…
but untouched by it.

Surrounded by light…
but still choosing darkness.

Knowing what God said…
but living like He didn’t.
Maybe that’s you.
You know what needs to change.

That relationship.
That habit.
That compromise.
That private sin nobody sees.
God already spoke.
You just haven’t moved.
This is where the Gospel confronts us.
Not gently.
Not vaguely.
Clearly.

You are not saved by hearing sermons.
You are not transformed by feeling convicted.
You are not made right by proximity to truth.
You are saved by Jesus Christ alone.
Because here’s the truth:
We didn’t just fail to obey.
We couldn’t.

Sin wasn’t just behavior.
It was our nature.

“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”
— Romans 3:23

That includes the listener.
That includes the churchgoer.
That includes the one who “knows better.”
But God didn’t leave us there.
He didn’t say, “Try harder.”
He sent Jesus.

Perfect obedience.
Sinless life.
A cross that carried every delayed obedience, every hidden sin, every spiritual excuse.

“Christ died for our sins in accordance with the Scriptures.”
— 1 Corinthians 15:3
And on that cross—
Jesus didn’t just forgive failure.
He broke its power.
So now the call is not:
“Listen more.”
The call is:
Repent. Believe. Follow.

Repent — turn from the sin you’ve been postponing.
Believe — trust that Jesus paid for it fully.
Follow — obey Him, not to earn salvation, but because you’ve been changed by it.
This is where shame meets redemption.
Because maybe you’re realizing right now:
“I’ve heard so much… but obeyed so little.”
Good.
That awareness?
That’s mercy.
Not condemnation.

“Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts.”
— Hebrews 3:15
Not tomorrow.
Not when it’s convenient.
Today.
You don’t need another sermon.
You need surrender.
You don’t need more knowledge.
You need a soft heart.
So here’s the question that will not leave you alone:
What has God already told you to do… that you are still delaying?
Name it.
Don’t spiritualize it.
Don’t excuse it.
Bring it to Jesus.
Because the same Jesus who warned about the falling house…
is the same Jesus who rebuilds broken lives.

Fully.
Freely.
Powerfully.
Right now—this is your moment.
Not to feel something.
To respond.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Joseph didn’t rise because of a dream.
paragraphs:
Joseph didn’t rise because of a dream.
He rose because he survived what the dream required.

Most people love Genesis 37.
The coat.
The visions.
The moment God reveals something extraordinary.
But very few are prepared for Genesis 39–40.

Because the dream is exciting…
but the process is offensive to comfort.

Joseph saw his future in a moment.
But he lived his preparation over years.
And here’s what many miss:

The dream wasn’t the destination.
It was the invitation into pressure.
The moment Joseph shared what God showed him, everything changed.

Favor turned into jealousy.
Family turned into betrayal.
And the place that should have protected him
became the place that rejected him.

Thrown into a pit.
Sold into slavery.
Falsely accused.
Forgotten in prison.
That doesn’t look like destiny.
But it was.

Because God was not just trying to show Joseph something.
He was trying to shape him into someone.

And what God shows you too early,
He will develop you slowly to sustain.

Joseph had a glimpse of authority…
but he needed the discipline to carry it.

He had a vision of leadership…
but he needed the humility to walk in it.

He saw people bowing…
but he first had to learn how to serve without recognition.
That’s the part we skip.

We want the palace.
But we resist the prison that prepares us for it.

We want influence.
But we avoid the hidden seasons that build integrity.

We want elevation.
But we don’t want the environments that expose our weaknesses.
Yet Joseph’s greatness wasn’t proven in the palace.
It was proven when no one was watching.

In Potiphar’s house, he chose integrity over opportunity (Genesis 39:9).
In prison, he served faithfully even when forgotten (Genesis 40:23).
Before Pharaoh, he gave God the credit instead of taking the spotlight (Genesis 41:16).

That’s not talent.
That’s transformation.

And here’s the truth most people don’t want to hear:
If Joseph had skipped the process,
he would have misused the promise.

Power without process produces pride.
Authority without character creates damage.
Promotion without preparation leads to collapse.
God wasn’t delaying Joseph.
He was protecting the future through the process.
Because one day, Joseph wouldn’t just manage resources.
He would hold the survival of nations in his hands.
And a man like that cannot be built overnight.

So God used the pit to break pride.
He used servanthood to build excellence.
He used false accusation to test purity.
He used prison to develop patience.

Every place that looked like a setback
was actually a classroom.
Every delay was a layer of strength.
Every hidden season was shaping visible impact.

And when the moment finally came—
when Pharaoh called him out of prison—
Joseph didn’t walk in as a dreamer.
He walked in as a man who had been refined.

He spoke with clarity.
He led with wisdom.
He stewarded with humility.
Because by then, the dream was no longer about him.
It was about purpose.

That’s when you know you’re ready—
when your dream stops being about your elevation
and starts being about God’s assignment.
Maybe that’s where you are right now.

Stuck in a season that doesn’t match what God showed you.
Praying, but not progressing.
Serving, but not seen.
Waiting, but not understanding.
But what if you’re not behind?
What if you’re being built?

What if the silence is strengthening your character?
What if the delay is developing your capacity?
What if the hidden place is preparing you for a visible assignment?
Because God doesn’t rush people into destiny.
He prepares them for it.

The pit is not your ending.
The prison is not your identity.
The process is not your punishment.
It’s preparation.

And if you stay faithful where you are,
God knows exactly when to move you forward.
Joseph didn’t chase the palace.
He honored God in the process.

And when the time was right,
God brought the palace to him.
So don’t despise your current season.

Because the same God who gave you the dream
is the same God shaping you to carry it.

Which part of Joseph’s journey are you in right now—
the dream, the pit, the prison, or the process?
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: He wasn’t lost.
paragraphs: He wasn’t lost.
You were.
That’s the tension in Gospel of Luke 2.
A twelve-year-old boy stands in the temple—dust in the air, ancient stone walls breathing history, scholars leaning in… listening.
Not correcting Him.
Listening.
Let that unsettle you.
Because while heaven was speaking in the temple, His parents were searching in the crowd.
Three days.
Three long, aching, panic-filled days.
Mary’s chest tight. Joseph scanning faces. Every shadow a disappointment.
“Where is He?”
And then—
They find Him.
Not wandering.
Not afraid.
Not confused.
Focused.
Sitting among teachers. Asking questions that pierced. Answering with wisdom that silenced grown men.
And then comes the line that slices through human expectation:
“Did you not know that I must be about My Father’s business?” — Luke 2:49 (NKJV)
Not harsh.
Not rebellious.
Revealing.
Jesus wasn’t dismissing Mary.
He was declaring identity.
At twelve… He already knew.

Who He was.
Whose He was.
Why He came.
And here’s the uncomfortable truth:
You can walk with Jesus for years… and still lose sight of Him.
Mary and Joseph didn’t abandon Him.
They assumed He was “with them.”
That’s where it gets dangerous.
Because assumption can replace devotion.
Routine can replace relationship.
Religion can replace revelation.
Let that sit.
How many of us are moving forward in life—career, relationships, ministry, dreams—thinking Jesus is “somewhere in the group”… while our direction has quietly drifted away from the Father’s will?
We look busy.
We sound spiritual.
But we haven’t actually checked if He’s with us.
That’s the warning in Luke 2.
But don’t miss the grace.
Because even when they misunderstood Him…
They found Him.
Even when they questioned Him…
He stayed with them.
Scripture says He went down with them and was subject to them (Luke 2:51).
The Son of God—perfect, pure, fully aware of His divine identity—chose submission.
Let that humble you.
He didn’t use His identity to rebel.
He used it to obey.
And that points us somewhere deeper.
This moment in the temple is not just a childhood story.
It’s a preview.
A whisper of what’s coming.
The same Jesus who said, “I must be about My Father’s business” would later walk straight into a cross.
Not by accident.
Not by pressure.
By purpose.
Because the Father’s business… was you.

Your sin.
Your wandering.
Your quiet compromises.
Your hidden guilt.
Your double life.
Your religious mask.
He saw all of it.
And still chose the cross.
The boy in the temple became the Lamb on the hill.
And on that cross, Jesus didn’t just answer questions…
He answered the problem of your soul.
Sin separated you from God.
No amount of effort, morality, or religion could close that gap.
But Jesus lived the life you couldn’t live—perfect, obedient, surrendered.
Then He died the death you deserved.
And three days later…
He rose.
So that lost people could be found.
Not in a temple.
But in Him.
Let me speak straight to your heart.
Some of you are like Mary and Joseph right now.
Anxious.
Disoriented.
Searching.
You’ve lost clarity.
Lost peace.
Maybe even feel like you’ve lost God.
But hear this:
He is not lost.
You just need to return.
Go back to where you last truly encountered Him.
Not the version of faith you perform online.
Not the routine you inherited.
The real place.

Where Scripture is open.
Where your heart is honest.
Where surrender is not theoretical.
Jesus is not hiding from you.
But He will not compete with everything else you keep choosing over Him.
And when you find Him…
You’ll realize something powerful:
He has always been about the Father’s business.
The question is—
Are you?
This is your moment.
Turn back.
Lay it down.
Drop the pride.
Confess the sin.
Release the illusion of control.
And come home.
Because the same Jesus in Luke 2…
Is still calling today.
Not just to admire Him.
But to follow Him.
To know the Father.
To live with purpose.
To walk in truth.
To be transformed by grace.
From lost… to found.
And if you’re ready—
Say it in your heart right now:
“Jesus, bring me back to the Father.”
Because He will.
He always does.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: The sky won’t whisper your name.
paragraphs:
The sky won’t whisper your name.
It will expose it.
And that’s what terrifies us.

Because deep down…
we already know what’s hiding in the dark.
You saw the lightning in that image.

That man—frozen between fear and realization—
isn’t just looking at the sky.
He’s seeing himself.
And maybe… so are you.
Because we’ve mastered the art of appearing okay.

Church face.
Filtered faith.
Polished words.
But hidden habits.

Secret compromises.
Silent sins we think no one notices.
And we tell ourselves, “Later. I’ll fix it later.”
But lightning doesn’t schedule appointments.
It interrupts.
It reveals.
It forces truth into the open.
Jesus didn’t describe His return gently.

In Matthew 24:27, He said:
“For as lightning comes from the east and shines as far as the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.”
No secrecy.
No delay.
No pretending.
And here’s where it hits hard—

Lightning doesn’t just light the sky.
It exposes everything underneath it.

The pride you justified.
The lust you hid.
The bitterness you fed.
The compromise you renamed as “normal.”
And suddenly, what was hidden… is undeniable.
That’s why the man in the image is trembling.
Not because lightning is loud—
But because truth is louder.
Let’s be honest.
We don’t fear God’s return because we don’t believe it.
We fear it because we know…
We’re not ready.
And here’s the tension:

God is not mocked.
Sin is not invisible.
And holiness is not optional.

Galatians 6:7 says:
“Do not be deceived: God is not mocked, for whatever one sows, that will he also reap.”
That’s not a threat.
That’s reality.

You plant secrecy—
you reap exposure.

You plant pride—
you reap distance from God.

You plant sin—
you reap death.

Romans 6:23 says it plainly:
“For the wages of sin is death…”
And that’s where most people stop.
Fear.
Guilt.
Shame.
But listen—
That’s not the full verse.
“…but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.”
There it is.
Grace.

Because the same God who warns you with lightning…
also reached for you with nails.
This is where everything shifts.
You don’t clean yourself up to meet Jesus.
You run to Him while you’re still exposed.
Because Jesus didn’t come for the polished.
He came for the honest.

1 John 1:9 says:
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.”
Not some sins.
All.
Not later.
Now.
But here’s what we miss—
Confession isn’t just saying “sorry.”
It’s surrender.
It’s dropping the mask.
It’s choosing truth over image.
And yes… it costs your pride.
But it saves your soul.
Some scholars interpret the “lightning” in Matthew 24 not only as speed and visibility, but as divine revelation—God making everything known in an instant.
No filters.
No edits.
Just truth.
So the question isn’t:
“Will He come?”
The question is:
What will His light reveal in you?

Because one day—
the sky will split.

And in that moment,
there will be two kinds of people:
Those who hide…
And those who run toward Him.
Not because they’re perfect—
But because they’re forgiven.
Because they’ve already stepped into the light before the lightning came.

John 3:19-21 says:
“Light has come into the world, and people loved the darkness rather than the light because their works were evil… But whoever does what is true comes to the light…”
Did you catch that?
Coming into the light is a choice.
Right now.
Not later.
Not when life is easier.
Not when you feel “ready.”
Now.
So let me ask you—
What are you still hiding?
What are you still delaying?
What are you still pretending God doesn’t see?
Because He does.
And yet—
He’s still calling you.
Not to shame you.
But to save you.
Jesus took your exposure on the cross.
Every sin.
Every secret.
Every failure.
Paid for.
In full.

So that when lightning comes—
you don’t have to fear judgment.
You can stand in grace.
This is your moment.
Not tomorrow.
Not someday.
Right now.
Drop the mask.
Confess the sin.
Turn your heart.
Run to Jesus.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: He was a king…
paragraphs:
He was a king…
but couldn’t control the war inside his own mind.

And the one thing that calmed him?
Was something he never learned to carry himself.
Read that again.

Saul had authority—but no peace.
A throne—but no rest.
Power in public… torment in private.

Scripture doesn’t hide it.
In 1 Samuel 16:14, it says the Spirit of the Lord departed from Saul, and a distressing spirit troubled him.
Let that sink in.

The real crisis wasn’t the demon.
It was the distance.
Distance from God.
And here’s the part we don’t like to admit—

You can look anointed…
and still be empty.

You can lead people…
and still be losing yourself.

You can sit in church…
and still be spiritually suffocating.
Because some of you know exactly what that feels like.

You worship publicly…
but secretly, your thoughts are loud, restless, unclean.

You pray occasionally…
but obedience is delayed.

You say “God is first”…
but your habits say otherwise.
And no one sees it.
Except God.
And you.
And the silence is getting heavier.
Here’s the tension—
Saul needed David to do what Saul himself refused to become.
A worshipper.
Every time David played, Scripture says in 1 Samuel 16:23 that relief came to Saul, and the torment left him.
Not because of talent.
But because of presence.
David carried what Saul abandoned.
AHA moment:

You don’t just need deliverance…
you need restored intimacy.

Because what you carry in private
will always manifest in public.
SPIRITUAL MIRROR:

If peace only comes when someone else is leading you into God’s presence…
you’ve stopped walking with Him yourself.
Let that confront you.

This is deeper than stress.
Deeper than mood swings.

This is what happens when calling is maintained…
but connection is neglected.
And here’s the uncomfortable truth—

Some people don’t need a breakthrough.
They need repentance.

Not louder worship songs.
Not more distractions.
Repentance.
Turning back.
Because the issue was never that God stopped being present.
It’s that Saul stopped honoring Him.
And slowly… subtly… dangerously…
His heart drifted.
Have you?
Be honest.

When was the last time you sat with God
without rushing?

When was the last time you obeyed immediately
instead of negotiating?

When was the last time your worship was real…
not routine?
Because delayed obedience is still disobedience.
And hidden compromise always grows louder over time.
But here’s where grace walks in—
God didn’t leave Saul without a witness.
He sent David.
A reminder.
A doorway back.

And today—
He’s sending you this.
Not to shame you.
To wake you up.

Because the same God who allowed David’s harp to calm a tormented king
sent His Son, Jesus Christ, to do something far greater.
Not just calm the noise.
Destroy the root.
Sin.
The Bible says in Romans 3:23 that all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.

That includes you.
That includes me.
But it doesn’t end there.
Because in Romans 5:8, God shows His love—while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.

Not when you fixed yourself.
Not when you cleaned up.
While you were still struggling.
Still hiding.
Still drifting.
And through the cross—
Jesus didn’t just play a song over your pain.
He paid for your freedom.
Full.
Final.
Finished.
So now the invitation isn’t “try harder.”
It’s “come back.”
Repent.
Return.
Restore the relationship you’ve been replacing with routine.
Because you were never created to survive off borrowed worship.
You were created to walk with God.
Identity shift:

You are not a spiritually exhausted performer.
You are a called, redeemed child of God.
But children stay close.
So come close again.
Right now.
No pretending.
No delay.
Just honesty.
“Lord… I’ve drifted.”
“Lord… I need You.”
“Lord… bring me back.”
And He will.
Because 1 John 1:9 promises—if we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us and cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
Not maybe.
Faithful.
This isn’t the end of your story.
It’s the turning point.
If this pierced your heart, don’t ignore it.
Take it.
Grow.
Stay anchored.
Next message?
We’re going deeper into why some people feel God less… even when they’re doing more.
Stay ready.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: King Asa’s story is one of the most uncomfortable warnings in the Bible.
paragraphs: King Asa’s story is one of the most uncomfortable warnings in the Bible.

Not because he started badly.
But because he started well.
He was a king who once trusted God deeply.

When an overwhelming army came against Judah, Asa did not run to alliances.
He did not search for political leverage.
He did not panic and build human strategies.
Instead, he prayed.
“And Asa cried unto the Lord his God…” (2 Chronicles 14:11)
He stood before God and said something powerful:
“Lord, it is nothing with you to help, whether with many, or with them that have no power.”
That was a king who understood dependence.
And God answered.

The enemy army was defeated.
The nation experienced peace.
Asa’s reign was marked by reform and spiritual restoration.
But years later, pressure returned.
And something had changed.
Instead of going back to the same God who gave him victory, Asa chose a different solution.

He took silver and gold from the temple treasury and sent it to the king of Syria.
He made a political alliance to solve a military problem.
And on the surface, it worked.
The enemy threat backed off.
The strategy succeeded.
But heaven was not impressed.
Because the issue was never just about the outcome.
It was about where Asa placed his trust.
God sent the prophet Hanani with a message that cuts deep even today:

“Because you relied on the king of Syria and not on the Lord your God… you have done foolishly.”
— 2 Chronicles 16:7
Think about that.

Asa didn’t abandon God publicly.
He didn’t build idols.
He didn’t deny the Lord.
He simply stopped trusting Him first.
And that is where the warning becomes personal.
Because many people today do the exact same thing.

They still talk about God.
They still believe in God.
They still remember what God did in the past.
But when pressure comes…

They trust money first.
Connections first.
Influence first.
Human solutions first.
Prayer becomes the last option instead of the first response.
That’s the quiet shift that destroyed Asa’s legacy.
The tragedy of his story is not failure at the beginning.
It’s drift in the middle.
One of the most dangerous moments in a believer’s life is not when they are desperate.
It’s when they become experienced.
Because experience can slowly replace dependence.
You start remembering strategies instead of remembering surrender.
You start calculating instead of trusting.
You start leaning on systems instead of leaning on God.

And suddenly the thing that once required faith…
is now handled by human control.
But God responded to Asa with a powerful reminder that still echoes today:

“For the eyes of the Lord run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to show Himself strong on behalf of those whose heart is fully committed to Him.”
— 2 Chronicles 16:9
Think about that image.
God is actively searching.

Not for the most powerful.
Not for the most connected.
Not for the most strategic.
But for the ones who still trust Him fully.

People whose first instinct is still prayer.
People whose confidence is still heaven.
People who refuse to replace God with human security.
Because the greatest danger to faith is rarely open rebellion.
Sometimes it is quiet replacement.
A slow shift.
A subtle drift.
A moment where alliances start looking safer than dependence.
King Asa reminds us of something every believer must guard carefully:

You can have a history with God
and still drift away from trusting Him.

You can remember past miracles
and still choose human solutions.

You can start in faith
and slowly slide into self-reliance.
That is why this story is not just history.
It is a mirror.
So the real question is not about Asa.
The real question is about us.
When pressure comes into your life…
Where does your trust run first?

Do you run to systems?
Or do you run to God?
Because the eyes of the Lord are still searching.
And He still shows Himself strong for those who trust Him fully.

Discussion Question:
What do you think is the modern version of Asa’s mistake today — trusting money, influence, connections, or something else?
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: You’re not too late. You’re being prepared.
paragraphs: You’re not too late. You’re being prepared.
Let that sink in for a moment.

Because one of the quietest fears people carry is this:
“I’m behind.”

Behind in life.
Behind in success.
Behind in purpose.
Behind in where everyone else seems to be.
You scroll through social media and it feels like everyone started the race before you.

Someone already built the business.
Someone already found their calling.
Someone already bought the house.
Someone already got married.
Someone already succeeded.
And there you are…
Standing at the starting line.
Watching the dust of everyone else’s footsteps fade into the distance.
It can make you question everything.
You start asking painful questions in the quiet moments:

“Did I miss my chance?”
“Did I start too late?”
“Did I waste too many years?”
“Did God forget about me?”
But here is a truth that can completely change how you see your life:
God does not measure your life by human timelines.
He measures it by purpose.

The world says:
“If you haven’t made it by now, you’re behind.”

God says:
“I am still writing your story.”

The world says:
“You should have started earlier.”

God says:
“I started preparing you earlier.”

The world says:
“You’re late.”

God says:
“You’re right on time.”
Here’s something powerful many people forget:
God often delays the start so He can strengthen the runner.
David waited years before becoming king.
Joseph spent years in prison before stepping into leadership.
Moses lived 40 years in the wilderness before God called him.
Even Jesus waited 30 years before beginning His public ministry.
Think about that.
The Son of God Himself did not rush His calling.
So why do we believe our timeline must look perfect?
The truth is this:

Sometimes God allows you to feel like the race already started…
so you stop trying to run someone else’s lane.
Because comparison is one of the fastest ways to lose your calling.
When you watch everyone else, you lose focus on the lane God gave you.
And the enemy loves that.
He whispers:

“You’re behind.”
“You’re late.”
“You missed it.”
But heaven says something different.
Heaven says:

“Wait for the Lord; be strong, and let your heart take courage; wait for the Lord!”
— Psalm 27:14
Waiting is not wasted.
Waiting is where God builds endurance.
Waiting is where He shapes your character.
Waiting is where He strengthens the faith you will need when the race gets hard.
The world celebrates speed.
But God values preparation.
Because when your moment finally comes, God doesn’t want you to just start the race…
He wants you ready to finish it.
And that’s why some people start earlier.
But you were being prepared.
Prepared for strength.
Prepared for resilience.
Prepared for purpose.
Prepared for a story that will impact more people than you realize.
Look closely at the image in this poster.
The runner isn’t panicking.
He isn’t quitting.
He isn’t walking away.
He’s doing something powerful.
He’s still at the starting line.
Still focused.
Still determined.
Still believing the race is worth running.
And maybe that’s exactly where you are right now.
You may feel like everyone else is ahead.
But God has not disqualified you.
Your race is not over.
Your lane is still open.
Your story is still unfolding.
The moment you step forward in faith…
everything can change.
Because with God, starting late does not mean finishing last.
Sometimes the runner who starts last finishes strongest.
And one day, you may look back and realize something incredible:
The delay that frustrated you…
was the preparation that saved you.
So if you feel behind in life right now, hear this clearly:

You are not forgotten.
You are not disqualified.
You are not too late.
You are being prepared.
Your race is still ahead.
And when God says go…
no lost time can stop what He planned for your life.

Someone in your life may need this reminder today.
Encourage them.
And if you’re in a season of waiting, I want to ask you something:
What is something you’re trusting God’s timing for right now?
Your story might be the encouragement someone else needs today.
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: THE CHARACTER I ALMOST OVERLOOKED: JABEZ
paragraphs: THE CHARACTER I ALMOST OVERLOOKED: JABEZ
There is a man in the Bible whose entire story is only two verses long.
Two verses.
Buried inside a genealogy most people skim past.

Most readers never notice him.
Most sermons rarely mention him.
Most Bible studies move right over his name.
But hidden in that list of names is one of the most powerful prayers ever recorded.
His name was Jabez.
And his story begins with pain.
Scripture says his mother named him Jabez because “I gave birth to him in pain.”

In ancient culture, names mattered deeply.
Names often carried identity, meaning, and expectation.
Imagine growing up with a name that literally reminded everyone of sorrow.
Every introduction carried a shadow.
Every time someone spoke his name, it echoed the story of pain that surrounded his beginning.

Some people inherit wealth.
Some inherit influence.
Jabez inherited a label.
But here is where his story changes.
Instead of accepting that label as destiny…
He prayed.
And not a casual prayer.
Not a polite prayer.
Not a quiet, routine prayer whispered out of habit.
Scripture says “Jabez cried out to the God of Israel.”
This was desperation.
This was a man who refused to let his beginning write the rest of his story.
And his prayer was bold.
“Oh, that You would bless me…”
Not just survival.
Not just endurance.
Blessing.
Favor.
Provision.
A future that looked different than his past.
Then he prayed something even more daring.
“Enlarge my territory.”
He was asking God for expansion.
Opportunity.
Influence.
Room to grow beyond the limitations that life had placed around him.
Then he prayed something many people forget to ask.
“Let Your hand be with me.”
Because Jabez understood something important:
Blessing without God’s presence can destroy a person.
Influence without God’s guidance can ruin a life.
Expansion without God’s hand can lead to pride.
So he asked for the one thing that matters more than any blessing…
The presence of God.
Then he prayed one more line.
“Keep me from harm so that I will be free from pain.”
Think about that for a moment.
A man born in pain asked God to break the cycle.
A man whose identity was shaped by sorrow asked God to rewrite the ending.
And the Bible records a stunning conclusion in just a few words.
“And God granted his request.”
That’s it.
No long explanation.
No dramatic story.
Just the quiet, powerful statement that heaven heard him.
Which means something profound for us today.
Your beginning does not have to become your destiny.
Your past does not have to dictate your future.
The label someone placed on you does not have the authority to define the rest of your life.
One prayer can interrupt a pattern.
One cry to God can break a generational story.
One moment of faith can change the direction of a legacy.
Jabez reminds us that sometimes the most powerful people in Scripture are not the ones with long chapters.
Sometimes the greatest impact comes from the ones who simply refuse to accept the identity the world gave them.
He refused to let pain define him.
He refused to let history trap him.
He refused to let his name become his future.
Instead, he took his pain to God.
And God answered.
Think about how many people today are carrying labels they never chose.
“You’ll never succeed.”
“You’re just like your family.”
“You’ll always struggle.”
“You’ll never change.”
But Jabez teaches us something powerful:
God has the authority to rewrite what life tried to name you.
Your story is not locked.
Your future is not sealed.
Your legacy is not finished.
Sometimes the most life-changing prayer is not long or complicated.
Sometimes it is simply a desperate heart saying:
“God… change the pattern.”
And heaven still responds to those prayers.
Because one desperate prayer can change a legacy.
Scripture

“Jabez cried out to the God of Israel, ‘Oh, that you would bless me and enlarge my territory! Let your hand be with me, and keep me from harm so that I will be free from pain.’ And God granted his request.”
— **1 Chronicles 4:9
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: He survived the fire…
paragraphs:
He survived the fire…
but almost lost himself in the silence.
Read that again.

Because this is where most people misunderstand Elijah.
And maybe—this is where you’re misunderstanding God right now.
Elijah just came from one of the most explosive moments in Scripture.

Fire fell from heaven.
Altars were consumed.
False prophets were exposed.

It was loud.
Undeniable.
Unforgettable.
God showed up in power.
But then—

One message.
One threat.
One voice from Jezebel.

And the man who called down fire…
ran for his life.
Let’s be honest.
You’ve had moments like that too.

Moments where your faith felt unshakable.
Where prayers were answered.
Where God felt close—almost tangible.
And then suddenly…

Fear hits.
Anxiety creeps in.
You start running.

Not from God—
but from everything else.
Elijah collapses under a broom tree and says something shocking:
“Lord, take my life.” (1 Kings 19:4)

This isn’t a weak man.
This is a weary man.
There’s a difference.

And if you don’t understand that—
you’ll misread the whole story.
Here’s what’s wild:
God doesn’t start with a sermon.
He starts with rest.

Food.
Water.
Sleep.

Again.
And again.

Before God speaks to Elijah’s calling—
He cares for Elijah’s condition.

Some of you are asking for direction…
while ignoring your exhaustion.
Then comes the cave.
Mount Horeb.
The place of encounter.
And this is where the expectation builds.

Because if God showed up in fire before—
surely He’ll do it again.
Right?
The wind comes.

Violent.
Rock-splitting.
Uncontainable.

But Scripture says—
the Lord was not in the wind.
Then the earthquake.

The ground shakes.
The mountain trembles.
Surely this is it.

But again—
the Lord was not in the earthquake.
Then fire.

Familiar.
Powerful.
Spectacular.
This is what Elijah knows.
But no—
the Lord was not in the fire.
Pause.
Because this is where most people stop reading carefully.
They assume God wasn’t present.
But Scripture doesn’t say God was absent.
It says He was not in those displays.
Meaning—
God was revealing something deeper.
Then comes the moment.

No explosion.
No spectacle.
No overwhelming force.
Just this:
“A still small voice.” (1 Kings 19:12)
A whisper.
And suddenly—
Elijah covers his face.
Why?
Because he recognizes it.

Not the volume.
But the presence.
Here’s the truth most people miss:

God didn’t lose His power.
He was revealing His heart.

Power gets your attention.
But intimacy transforms your life.
Some of you are addicted to spiritual noise.

You want the big sign.
The viral moment.
The emotional high.
But God is not trying to impress you.
He’s trying to draw you close.

Because the deepest encounters with God
are not always the loudest ones.

They’re the quiet moments
where everything else fades—
and it’s just you and Him.
And this points us straight to Jesus.
Because God didn’t just whisper once on a mountain—
He stepped into human history in silence.

No thunder.
No announcement to kings.
Just a baby in a manger.
Quiet.
Hidden.
Holy.
And when Jesus went to the cross—
There was no spectacle to save Him.

No fire from heaven.
No earthquake to rescue Him in that moment.

Just suffering.
Stillness.
Silence.
Why?
Because He was carrying your sin.

Your fear.
Your running.
Your exhaustion.
So when God speaks now—
You don’t have to fear His voice.

Because that voice
has already chosen mercy over judgment.

That whisper
has already spoken forgiveness through the blood of Christ.
Maybe the reason you’re not hearing God…
is not because He’s silent.
But because you’re listening for the wrong volume.
Turn down the noise.

The scrolling.
The pressure.
The expectations.
The chaos in your mind.
And lean in.

Because the same God
who commanded fire from heaven—

is the same God
who sits close enough to whisper your name.
You are not abandoned.
You are being invited.
And that whisper?
It’s not weak.
It’s personal.
If this spoke to you, don’t keep it to yourself.

Someone you know is exhausted, overwhelmed,
and waiting for God to shout—
when He’s already speaking.
And tonight—
before you sleep—
get quiet.
Even for a minute.
And listen.
“After the fire came a gentle whisper.” — 1 Kings 19:12
author: Gospel Warrior (John Domino Sanchez Asis)

title: Heaven skipped the palace… and chose a village nobody respected.
paragraphs: Heaven skipped the palace… and chose a village nobody respected.
Bethlehem.
Small. Dusty. Forgotten.
There was a boy there once.

Not famous.
Not followed.
Not even invited.
His name was David.

While others stood tall in front of the prophet, polished and prepared, David was out in the fields—hands rough, skin marked by sun and wind, the scent of sheep clinging to him like a label he didn’t choose.
And yet… God chose him.

Not because he looked like a king.
But because his heart belonged to the King.
That moment turned Bethlehem into something more than a town.
It became the City of David.
But that wasn’t the end of the story.
That was the setup.
Because God made a promise that didn’t make sense at first:
